stories.headline: PM Modi speaks to Zelenskyy, offers India's help in peaceful resolution of Ukraine war
stories.title: PM Modi speaks to Zelenskyy, offers India's help in peaceful resolution of Ukraine war
stories.summary: PM Modi speaks to Zelenskyy, offers India's help in peaceful resolution of Ukraine war
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed

opening: New Delhi, Nov 9: Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a telephonic conversation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday during which Modi conveyed India's readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict with Russia.
PM Modi also reaffirmed India's human-centric approach and reiterated India's consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.
body: The prime minister conveyed India's readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at the peaceful resolution of the conflict, a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
During the telephonic conversation, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments related to the ongoing conflict.
The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors for the mutual benefit of the two peoples.
"Glad to have had a productive telephone conversation with President Zelenskyy.

We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties," PM Modi said on X. "I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace.
Reiterated India’s firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution," he said.
In August, Zelenskyy said Kyiv was counting on "India's contribution to ending the war with Russia".
Zelenskyy, in a social media post, said Ukraine appreciates India's dedication to "peace and dialogue".
"Now, as the entire world strives to end this horrible war with dignity and lasting peace, we count on India's contribution," Zelenskyy said.
In October, Russian President Vladimir Putin had said Modi has "very good ideas" on a mutual settlement of the Ukraine conflict and raises the issue at "every meeting".

"As for Prime Minister Modi's position on ending wars, I can say that he is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good, even friendly relations, including at the personal level, constantly raises the issue and asks questions about ending the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.

Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov has also said that India has declared its readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the Ukraine conflict and Russia is grateful to New Delhi for such readiness and the ideas.
Ukraine President Zelenskyy shares his perspective on recent developments in the ongoing conflict.

stories.headline: Kerala HC directs Sanskrit varsity to produce email linked to deferral of campus election
stories.title: Kerala HC directs Sanskrit varsity to produce email linked to deferral of campus election
stories.summary: Petitioner sought to quash the postponement order and have the election conducted as originally scheduled
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Kerala High Court recently directed Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS), Kalady, to produce an email that allegedly led to the deferral of the campus union election.

Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan was considering a petition filed by Union general secretary candidate P.K. Midhun Krishna, alleging that the Vice-Chancellor (V-C) had postponed the election solely on the basis of complaints from students reportedly affiliated with the Akhila Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Kerala Students Union (KSU).
The petitioner claimed that the complainants had submitted their nominations to contest the election, but these were rejected due to defects in their applications.
The petition stated that the V-C had cited a report by the impartial observer (IO) of the campus election recommending the postponement in her order.
However, the petitioner claimed that the IO had not recommended postponing the polls and had allegedly communicated this to the returning officer.
Mr. Krishna, a postgraduate student at the university, informed the court that he and some other students had approached the V-C seeking a review of the postponement order.
Aggrieved by the V-C’s inaction on their request, the petitioner had moved the High Court.
The petitioner sought to quash the postponement order and have the election conducted as originally scheduled.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently directed the State of Uttar Pradesh to carry out an exercise identifying all undertrial prisoners in 55 districts who have been granted bail but have not been released due to failure to comply with bail conditions, including execution of sureties.

The Court has stated that the exercise would cover all undertrial prisoners irrespective of whether they have engaged a private lawyer or have sought assistance of the District Legal Services Authority(DLSA).
Further, it must be carried out with the help of the concerned DLSA.

A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale passed these directions in a suo motu matter in which the issue related to the release of undertrials who haven't been released due to their unwillingness or inability to furnish bail sureties.
The bench made clear that this can't be an adversarial litigation where benefit is only extended to those who are being given assistance of NALSA.
"This direction shall be applicable even to those under-trial prisoners who could not comply with the bail conditions, despite the fact that they have engaged the private lawyers.
There cannot be any differentiation between the under-trial prisoners, who have the assistance of District Legal Services Authority and those who have engaged private counsel."
The orders were passed after hearing the submissions made by the Senior Advocate for the State of Uttar Pradesh, Pradeep Mishra, counsel for NALSA and the petitioners.
It was informed to the Court that in UP, there are 264 undertrial prisoners who have been granted bail, out of which only 158 have been released.
106 prisoners are yet to be released due to the want of execution of sureties, or other conditions imposed by the Trial Court.
It was further informed that the 264 prisoner statistic is only for 20 districts.
NALSA is yet to carry out such exercise of identifying undertrials in 55 districts.

stories.headline: Supreme Court: Public servant in custody over 48 hours is deemed suspended
stories.title: Supreme Court: Public servant in custody over 48 hours is deemed suspended
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: If a public servant is arrested and kept in judicial custody for more than 48 hours, there is a deemed suspension, the Supreme Court has said.
A bench comprising Justices J B Pardiwala and Manmohan made the observation while restoring the bail granted to Vishwajeet Singh, the administrator of Sadar Hospital at Samastipur in Bihar.
Singh was accused of demanding a bribe of Rs 4,000 for clearing a contractual worker's pending wages of Rs 36,421.
The top court set aside a Patna High Court order cancelling his bail nearly a year after it was granted.
The bench said that although the amount of bribe demanded was not a relevant consideration for deciding a bail plea, the high court could have made that observation without cancelling the bail.
While restoring the bail, the apex court also flagged a "disturbing feature" concerning the accused's service status and subsequent posting.
"However, there is one disturbing feature which we should not ignore.
It appears that upon arrest, the appellant accused was in judicial custody for almost a period of 15 days.
"Once a public servant is arrested and remains in judicial custody for more than 48 hours, there is a deemed suspension.
Being a public servant, he could be said to have been placed under deemed suspension.
No specific order is required to be passed in this regard," Justice Pardiwala said in the order dated November 6.
The bench noted the information that Singh was placed under suspension but later, the suspension order came to be revoked.

opening: Capital markets regulator Sebi has given the go-ahead to six companies, including Coal India subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields, Veritas Finance, Sagar Defence Engineering and Encube Ethicals, to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs), paving the way for a fresh round of public issues across the financial services, defence, pharmaceutical and jewellery sectors.
The other two companies that have received regulatory clearance are IFL Finance and Arjun Jewellers, according to Sebi's latest processing status of draft offer documents.
body: The six companies filed their preliminary IPO papers between July and September 2026 and received the market regulator's observations between October 15 and November 4.
In Sebi's terminology, issuing observations on draft offer documents allows companies to proceed with their IPO plans.
The companies will announce their issue dates, price bands and other details closer to their respective launches.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPOMahanadi Coalfields, a wholly owned subsidiary of state-run Coal India, plans to enter the stock market through an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 66.18 crore equity shares by its parent company.
The proposed IPO will consist entirely of existing shares, meaning.
Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the public issue.
The company filed its draft papers on September 3, with SBI Capital Markets serving as the lead manager.
Mahanadi Coalfields, incorporated in 1992, is one of India's major coal producers, operating primarily in Odisha.
The company produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal during FY26, accounting for approximately 22.4% of India's non-coking coal production, according to industry data cited in its draft prospectus.
Sagar Defence Engineering IPODefence technology company Sagar Defence Engineering has received Sebi's approval for its proposed IPO, which is estimated to be worth around Rs 3,000 crore.
The company submitted its preliminary documents on August 6 through Sebi's confidential pre-filing route, with JM Financial acting as the coordinating lead manager.
The regulator issued its observations on November 4.
Sagar Defence develops advanced defence and aerospace technologies, including unmanned systems and autonomous platforms.

The proposed listing comes amid growing investor interest in India's defence manufacturing sector, supported by government initiatives to encourage domestic production and reduce dependence on imported military equipment.
As the company opted for confidential pre-filing, the final issue structure and detailed offer terms will become clearer when it publishes its updated offer documents.
Encube Ethicals IPOSpecialty pharmaceutical company.
Encube Ethicals has received Sebi's clearance for its proposed Rs 3,000 crore IPO.

The public issue will consist entirely of an offer for sale by promoter Mehul Madhusudan Shah and existing shareholder Frontier Investment Holdings, which is backed by private equity firm Quadria Capital.
Shah plans to sell shares worth up to Rs 2,000 crore, while Frontier Investment Holdings intends to offload shares worth Rs 1,000 crore.
Since the offering consists entirely of existing shares, Encube Ethicals will not receive any proceeds from the IPO.
The Mumbai-based company operates in pharmaceutical formulations, global generics and contract development and manufacturing services.
It has manufacturing facilities in Goa and Indore.
For FY26, Encube Ethicals reported a 75% rise in net profit to Rs 436.7 crore, while revenue increased 34.7% to Rs 1,848.7 crore.

Veritas Finance IPOChennai-based non-banking financial company Veritas Finance plans to raise Rs 900 crore through a fresh issue of shares, alongside an offer for sale of up to 1.28 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.
The company, backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital, filed its revised draft papers in July and received Sebi's observations on October 19.
The proposed IPO marks Veritas Finance's second attempt at entering the stock market.
It had earlier received regulatory clearance in April 2025 for a Rs 2,800 crore IPO, comprising a Rs 600 crore fresh issue and an OFS worth Rs 2,200 crore.
However, the company did not proceed with the offering.
Under the revised plan, Veritas Finance may also undertake a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 180 crore.
If completed, the fresh issue size will be reduced accordingly.
The company intends to use the fresh issue proceeds to strengthen its capital base and support future lending requirements.
Veritas Finance primarily provides loans to micro, small and medium enterprises and self-employed individuals.
Its assets under management stood at Rs 9,134 crore as of March 2026, while its FY26 net profit was approximately Rs 330 crore.
ICICI Securities is the coordinating lead manager for the proposed issue.
IFL Finance IPOGold loan-focused non-banking financial company.
IFL Finance has received Sebi's clearance for its proposed IPO, comprising a fresh issue of up to 3.55 crore equity shares and an offer for sale of up to 30 lakh shares by existing shareholders.
The New Delhi-based lender filed its preliminary IPO documents on July 29 and received the regulator's observations on October 21.
The company plans to use the fresh issue proceeds to strengthen its Tier-I capital base, meet future lending requirements and comply with capital adequacy norms.
Aryaman Financial Services is the coordinating lead manager for the issue.
Arjun Jewellers IPOArjun Jewellers has also secured Sebi's approval to launch its proposed Rs 200 crore IPO.
The public issue will consist entirely of fresh equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component.
The company intends to use the proceeds primarily to meet additional working capital requirements, including the purchase of inventory for existing and proposed retail showrooms.
A portion of the funds will also be used for general corporate purposes.
Arjun Jewellers submitted its draft papers on August 1, with Saffron Capital Advisors acting as the lead manager.
Sebi issued its observations on November 4.

stories.headline: Government putting transmitters in border areas to block international network: Sources
stories.title: Government putting transmitters in border areas to block international network: Sources
stories.summary: Customers near the border areas such as Ladakh, Sikkim and others had complained of telcos billing them of the network they haven’t used
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The government is working on penetrating transmitters in all the border areas of the country to block mobile networks of the neighbouring countries, which was an issue for years and several customers complained of getting cross-connections with other global networks without their knowledge.
“There were several complaints from consumers of cross connection near the border States like the Northeast and Ladakh.
But, transmitters are being put up in those areas soon, to block those network.
Wireless Planning and Coordination Wing (WPC) of the Department of Telecommunications is working on the project,” a senior government official told businessline.
WPC is the national radio regulatory authority of India, under the DoT.
Till four-five years back, the Indian mobile network service were not available in locations near the borders, as telcos were required to fade out signals just ahead of the border.
However, the DoT in August 2022 amended the licence norms to remove restrictions on telecom connectivity near international border areas, paving the way for better mobile coverage in these locations.

While, the amendment removed restrictions on telecom connectivity near international border areas, at the same time there were instances of mobile service switching over to international roaming automatically and customers complaining of telcos billing them of the network they haven’t used.

Earlier this year, there have been reports of customers getting international roaming charges billed after their mobile phones reportedly picked up a Chinese network signal during their visit to Nathu La pass in Sikkim, which sparked fresh concerns of border-area telecom coverage and billing practices.

In the past also, users have experienced getting text messages saying “Welcome to Bangladesh” while on trips to border areas of Assam and Meghalaya, and have been charged for international roaming from their mobile service providers.

“That is why these transmitters are being installed in all the base stations near the borders to curb their networks or relay back their radiowaves, so that such signals do not interfere with our networks...
WPC is working on it and it’s just a matter of a few days,” the official added.

stories.headline: The Man Saving Kashmir's Dying Lakes | Manzoor Wangnoo - Green Ambassador of Kashmir
stories.title: The Man Saving Kashmir's Dying Lakes | Manzoor Wangnoo - Green Ambassador of Kashmir
stories.summary: He was mentioned by PM Modi in Mann Ki Baat. They call him the Green Ambassador of Kashmir. But today, he is fighting alone. This is Manzoor Wangnoo - a businessman turned conservationist. The man who took a pledge for zero polythene in Gilsar, Khushalsar, Nigeen and succeeded. Now he is on a new mission - to save Anchaar, a lake he calls an orphan. Once sprawling across nearly 20 square kilometres, Anchar Lake has shrunk to barely 4.5 square kilometres, with a substantial portion of its remaining area reduced to marshland. In this exclusive conversation with Sarosh Kafeel, Manzoor Wangnoo speaks openly about the land mafia encroaching Anchaar, the support from the administration, and how he approached the present government and the CM but got no response. He warns that if Anchaar is not cleaned, Kashmir will face a flood-like situation again. The damage is so big, it will take at least a decade to clean it. His message is clear - youngsters have to come out and save this orphan lake before it's too late. Host: Sarosh Kafeel
